# Practical protocol: Predicting discontinuous B-cell epitopes with ELLIPro for an in silico multiepitope vaccine

## What ELLIPro predicts and how it works
ELLIPro identifies discontinuous (conformational) B‑cell epitopes on proteins by modeling the protein as an ellipsoid, computing a protrusion index (PI) for each residue, and clustering nearby residues with high PI to form putative epitopes; predicted epitopes receive a PI-based score reflecting their expected surface exposure and discontinuity characteristics.<cite id="eb97bcb5-3">ELLIPro identifies discontinuous B‑cell epitopes by approximating protein shape as an ellipsoid, computing a protrusion index for each residue, and grouping adjacent residues with similar PI values; this framework has been benchmarked against structural epitopes.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-8">ELLIPro uses neighbor residue clustering, residue-level protrusion index, and protein shape to rank epitopes, with default settings of 6 Å maximum distance and a minimum score of 0.5.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-9">ELLIPro uses residue clustering with Thornton's method and assigns protrusion index values to residues composing epitopes.</cite>

## Input, parameters, and outputs
On the IEDB ELLIPro server, you submit a protein sequence or structure; the server predicts sets of discontinuous epitopes with a confidence score derived from the PI across the epitope residues, allowing you to filter by minimum score and clustering distance.<cite id="eb97bcb5-7">Users submit a protein structure to ELLIPro; the server computes a protrusion index score for each predicted epitope and ranks them in descending order, with default options of minimum score 0.5 and clustering distance 6 Å.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-5">Default parameters on the server (e.g., minimum score 0.5 and maximum score 0.6) are commonly retained for conformational epitope prediction in multiepitope vaccine design.</cite>

In practice, many studies retain default or conservative thresholds (e.g., minimum score ≥0.5–0.6) and sometimes require higher PI within the epitope (e.g., PI >0.9) to emphasize highly protruding/surface-exposed regions.<cite id="eb97bcb5-5">Default parameters (minimum score 0.5, maximum score 0.6) are often used for ELLIPro in vaccine design.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-6">Some workflows select conformational epitopes with a high protrusion index cutoff (e.g., PI > 0.9) to prioritize surface-exposed discontinuous epitopes.</cite>

## Typical cutoffs and filters used in vaccine design studies
When selecting epitopes for multiepitope constructs, investigators commonly apply score-based and PI-based filters (e.g., ELLIPro score >0.5–0.6; PI >0.9) and sometimes corroborate predictions with additional predictors (e.g., DiscoTope) to reduce false positives.<cite id="eb97bcb5-6">Researchers using ELLIPro often select epitopes with PI > 0.9 and cross-check with DiscoTope for confirmation.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-5">Keeping default thresholds (e.g., minimum score 0.5, maximum 0.6) is common in vaccine design applications.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-7">EliPro outputs epitope scores based on PI, enabling ranking and selection under specified thresholds (e.g., min score 0.5, 6 Å clustering).</cite>

## Performance and validation considerations
ELLIPro has demonstrated favorable performance on benchmark datasets of conformational epitopes from antibody–protein complexes, with reported AUC around 0.732 when considering the strongest prediction per protein, indicating reasonable but not perfect discrimination of true epitopes.<cite id="eb97bcb5-3">On a benchmark dataset derived from 3D structures of antibody–protein complexes, ELLIPro achieved an AUC of approximately 0.732 for conformational epitope prediction using the strongest prediction per protein.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-8">ElliPro's reported AUC is about 0.732 at default options (6 Å, 0.5 min score), reflecting competitive performance among structure-based predictors.</cite>

Accuracy depends on the quality of the input structural model or experimental structure; inaccurately predicted or low-resolution structures can reduce the reliability of ELLIPro's epitope predictions, so if using a predicted structure, validate with experimental data or alternative predictors where possible.<cite id="eb97bcb5-4">The precision of ELLIPro is contingent on the integrity of the input protein structure; inaccuracies or low resolution can diminish reliability.</cite>

## Step-by-step workflow for your multiepitope vaccine project
1) Prepare your target protein(s) sequence(s) and obtain a structural model or use an experimentally determined structure. If using a predicted model, plan to validate with additional evidence or alternative predictors.<cite id="eb97bcb5-4">Prediction quality depends on input structure integrity; low-resolution or inaccurate models can reduce reliability.</cite>
2) Run the IEDB ELLIPro server with your sequence/structure and default or conservative thresholds (e.g., minimum score 0.5–0.6; residue clustering distance around 6 Å).<cite id="eb97bcb5-7">Default ELLIPro settings include minimum score 0.5 and 6 Å clustering distance.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-5">Default thresholds are often retained in vaccine design applications.</cite>
3) Extract predicted discontinuous epitopes and their PI-based scores. Sort by score and apply additional filters if desired (e.g., PI >0.9 to bias toward highly protruding epitopes).<cite id="eb97bcb5-8">ElliPro reports scores based on protrusion index; default thresholds are 6 Å and 0.5.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-6">PI cutoffs like >0.9 are used to emphasize surface-exposed epitopes.</cite>
4) Consider cross-validating with a second structure-based predictor (e.g., DiscoTope) to reduce false positives before assembling your multiepitope sequence.<cite id="eb97bcb5-6">Cross-checking with DiscoTope is commonly used to corroborate ELLIPro predictions.</cite>
5) Select a subset of non-overlapping epitopes that meet your quality thresholds and diversity goals for the vaccine construct, and proceed to antigenicity/immunogenicity analyses.

## Notes on interpretation and limitations
ELLIPro's score reflects epitope surface exposure via PI; high scores generally indicate more likely discontinuous epitopes on the protein surface, but the overall AUC suggests moderate discriminative power and thus value in ranking rather than absolute acceptance of single predictions.<cite id="eb97bcb5-7">ELLIPro ranks epitopes by PI-based scores, with higher scores indicating greater epitope potential on the surface.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-3">Benchmark performance shows AUC around 0.732, supporting ranking utility rather than definitive truth.</cite>

If your project requires linear (continuous) B‑cell epitopes as a complement, note that ELLIPro targets discontinuous epitopes, and linear epitope predictors such as BCPred/ABCpred are typically used side-by-side in multiepitope vaccine design workflows.<cite id="eb97bcb5-0">In multiepitope vaccine design, linear B‑cell epitopes are often predicted with BCPred while discontinuous epitopes are predicted with ELLIPro.</cite> <cite id="eb97bcb5-1">Linear and discontinuous epitopes are commonly selected using different predictors (e.g., BCPred/ABCpred for linear; ELLIPro for discontinuous) and common cutoffs/immunological filters.</cite>
